baseline.title: Historical FP9 lung timer baseline
baseline.research_question: Can the published FP9 localization, message-assembly, and external-report timeline be reproduced causally without adding fingerprint logic to the simulation kernel or lung model?

population.residual_rule: Historical allocation: 111 locators per target; the unassigned remainder is not used to alter the published FP9 first-event times.

sources.citation: R. Wendt, MEHLISSA dissertation, Chapter 6, Tables 6.3-6.5 and Section 6.5.2.
R. Wendt et al., Proteome Fingerprinting as a Localization Scheme for Nanobots, NANOCOM 2023.

limitations: The first-localization and external-report values are published outputs of the historical MEHLISSA abstraction, not independent physiological observations.
The baseline replays a deterministic timer and does not model gene-product concentration, binding, tile diffusion, message decay, collector encounter probability, or gateway radio physics.
The dissertation defines external-report time from injection through collection and wrist reporting; it does not publish separate collection and post-collection return times.
The historical wrist-readout latency is omitted as an assumed constant and must not be interpreted as measured zero latency.
The two collector cohorts are independent published regression cases; the timer replay is not a predictive interpolation law for other collector counts.
